The canonical form for the Layer-2 architectural concept is 'Layer-2' (prose: 'Layer 2'). 'truth_store' is not a listed allowed or discouraged variant — it is an undeclared net-new term. Critically, it introduces Category A governance-sensitive drift: 'Snapshot Truth' (SNAPSHOT_TRUTH) is already a canonical term for a distinct concept; 'truth_store' risks conflation with snapshot storage semantics and would blur the snapshot-boundary identity that Section 6 of CLAUDE.md declares non-negotiable. The term does not appear in any canonical document and cannot be adopted without a contract-affecting documentation change triggering all seven canonical document reviews (CLAUDE.md Section 11).

Proposed replacement term 'decision_layer' is unrecognized by the canonical term table. The canonical form is 'Layer-3' (prose: 'Layer 3'). 'decision_layer' is not a listed allowed or discouraged variant. Additionally it introduces Category D drift: 'decision_layer' lexically resembles the discouraged variant 'decision engine' listed under LAYER_3 and risks conflation with the decision-output vocabulary cluster (DecisionPacket, guard taxonomy, trigger taxonomy).

ambiguity_flags.note: The proposed term 'truth_store' would simultaneously evoke three distinct canonical concepts: the Layer-2 architectural layer (LAYER_2), the 'Snapshot Truth' concept (SNAPSHOT_TRUTH — a canonical term for what the snapshot boundary produces), and the 'snapshots' database table (SNAPSHOTS_TABLE). This three-way ambiguity would make it structurally harder to classify snapshot-boundary claims correctly in downstream governance steps. Category A governance-sensitive drift: any confusion about what enforces the snapshot contract is a hard failure condition per CLAUDE.md Section 6 (non-negotiable) and Section 7 (fail-closed).

The proposed term 'decision_layer' maps ambiguously to two distinct scopes: (1) the entire Layer-3 planned architectural tier, and (2) the 'Decision Engine' — a specific named planned component within Layer-3 (CLAUDE.md Section 3.2). Using 'decision_layer' as a synonym for the full layer risks conflation with the component-level Decision Engine vocabulary. Compound risk: if downstream documents reference 'decision_layer' when describing the Decision Engine component and 'decision_layer' when describing the full tier, inter-document consistency checks will have no stable referent. Category B and D governance-sensitive drift.
